newsitem.title: LIBERIA: African monitors say Liberia disarmament too slow.
newsitem.headline: African monitors say Liberia disarmament too slow.

text.p: A team of West African monitors of Liberia's peace process said on Saturday that its rival militias were disarming too slowly.

Nigeria Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi, heading the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) team, told a news conference in Monrovia that too few fighters had disarmed and that the quality and quantity of weapons handed in was poor.
"We are concerned at the numerical level of the men disarmed and the quantity and quality of arms collected so far," he said.
The deadline for disarmament of the estimated 60,000 fighters under a peace deal agreed in Nigeria's capital Abuja last August is January 31, in preparation for elections in May.
Monitors say that since the disarmament exercise began on November 22 less than 9,000 fighters have demobilised.

West African leaders who brokered the latest deal threatened sanctions against anyone derailing it. A dozen previous deals to end the war, which began in 1989 and has killed well over 150,000 people, collapsed.

Ikimi said Liberia's interim ruling council of state, which on Thursday held its first full session since shooting at the presidential mansion in October, had assured his team "that the meeting signalled a turn for the better".
Faction leaders Charles Taylor and Alhaji Kromah are vice-chairmen on the council.

"We count on the renewed commitment now given to us by the faction leaders that within the next few weeks, we would witness a substantial turn over of weapons and demobilisation of their fighters," he said.
